newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH STATE AUDITORS WORRIED BY STATE DEBT COSTS.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH STATE AUDITORS WORRIED BY STATE DEBT COSTS.

text.p: Finnish state debt and debt servicing costs will go on rising for many years and severely restrict the fiscal policy room to manoueuvre, the auditors of the state finances said on Thursday.

"The auditors ... think that the future trend of the state debt is very worrying when taking into account the effect on state revenue and expenditure of high unemployment and the growing state debt servicing costs," they said in their report on the 1995 state finances.
"State debt servicing will cause in the next few years ever growing annual costs," they said.
"State debt servicing costs will for many years impose substantial restrictions on fiscal policy," they added.

For many years to come, the state would be forced to pile up new debt simply in order to pay interest on existing debts, the report said, noting that next year, state debt servicing costs would account for 94 percent of new state net borrowing.
The nominal amount of state debt would go on growing unless tax revenue rose or state spending could be cut so much that debt servicing would be possible without new net borrowing.
"In the view of the state auditors, the government should make and bring to parliament a long-term programme to stop the increase in state debt and the costs linked to it," they said.
According to finance ministry projections, the state debt would rise to 438.2 billion markka by the end of 1997 while Finnish GDP would rise to about 600 billion markka, the report said.

State debt would rise to 73 percent of GDP in 1997 from 71.9 percent expected at end-1996, and then fall slightly to 72 percent in 1998. A chief government target is to bring state debt relative to GDP into decline.
